key_insight: A PT-symmetric altermagnetic topological-insulator heterostructure can produce a pure spin bulk photovoltaic effect, enabling dc spin currents without charge currents when symmetry suppresses charge photocurrent pathways.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a symmetry-tunable platform for spintronic optoelectronic devices that convert light directly into controllable spin currents with minimal charge dissipation.
method: Built a 2D heterostructure of a topological insulator coupled to a d-wave altermagnet.
Developed a non-Abelian spin-BPVE theory for PT-degenerate band manifolds.
Studied how Néel-vector orientation changes topology and nonlinear optical response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports symmetry-based analysis showing that in the xy-plane orientation C2z symmetry eliminates second-order charge photocurrents while leaving finite spin photocurrents, and that response sign reverses when the local Dirac mass changes sign.
watch_item: The pure spin output depends sensitively on maintaining the required symmetry and magnetic orientation, so real-device disorder, symmetry breaking, or imperfect Néel-vector control could reintroduce charge currents.
paper_title: Pure Spin Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in an Altermagnetic Higher-Order Topological Insulator
